publiccomments:
On July 16, 2025, a lake service provider reached out to MN DNR staff after finding what appeared to be zebra mussels on a lake residents dock on Cedar Lake, Scott County. The lake service provider took photos of the finding, and it was confirmed to be a zebra mussel by an Invasive Species Specialist at the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources.

On July 18, 2025, a contractor performed a zebra mussel search using snorkel and scuba. The total search time was one hour, no zebra mussels were found. On July 29, 2025, MN DNR Invasive Species staff took two water samples from Cedar Lake to detect veligers. Three veligers were detected under the microscope within the water samples.

The adult zebra mussels and veligers found at Cedar Lake, Scott County indicate in-lake spawning and a reproducing population. Cedar Lake has been added to DNR Infested Waters List for zebra mussels.

publiccomments: On 5/29/25, a watercraft inspector reported a single zebra mussel attached to aquatic vegetation on a watercraft leaving Big Marine Lake. The MnDNR and WCD visited the lake several times following this finding to survey the lake for zebra mussel presence. On 8/7/25, the MnDNR performed a veliger tow and found a juvenile zebra mussel present in one of the water samples. These results indicate the presence of a reproductive population in Big Marine Lake. Due to this finding, this waterbody has been added to the DNR Infested Waters List.

comments: On September 23, 2022 one 8mm (adult) zebra mussels was observed during a routine settlement plate check by Three Rivers Park District. They notified the MnDNR AIS staff the day of the observation. Additional searches were conducted on October 6, 2022 by MnDNR and 3RPD staff by wading, aquascope and SCUBA. Four locations were searched resulting in more than 25 adults and juvenile zebra mussels observed throughout the entire lake. Fish Lake in Hennepin County will be placed on the infested waters list for having zebra mussels.

locality: South Public Access Fishing Pier on Long Lake, Hubbard County, near Park Rapids, MN
comments: 1 potential zebra mussel found clasping aquatic vegetation during a training session on AIS & aquatic vegetation identification on weeds sampled by rake from the fishing pier for training.   The aquatic vegetation from the rake tosses was placed in white tubs for separation / identification during training.  Training was in preparation for aquatic vegetation monitoring to be conducted by boat peering into the water, looking for invasive species for early detection and meandering in their Long Lake Neighborhood in Littoral Area for mid-July and mid-August.  Training for the 3 participants was being offered by two lakeshore owners who are MAISRC / UMExt AIS Detectors - Jim Blodgett and Sharon Natzel.  We tried additional rake tosses from all directions at the fishing pier at the end of class to see if we could duplicate finding more of the potential zebra mussels but did not find any more.

locality: Long Lake, Ramsey County
reporter: Keegan Lund , Minnesota Department of Natural Resources
comments: On September 8, 2019 Noah and Mathew Berg (Endangered Resource Services, LLC) were performing an early detection zebra mussel survey. Noah Berg located a zebra mussel attached to a native mussel north east of the public boat launch on Long Lake. The survey effort is part of an early detection program organized by Ramsey County.  On September 12, 2019 DNR and Ramsey County staff surveyed around the access in an effort to detect more zebra mussels. There were two divers, one person snorkeling, and one wading in the shallows. After a 60 minute search effort, no zebra mussels were detected near the public access. The search was conducted in 1-8 feet of water, with most effort concentrated in 1-4 feet. On the day of the search, water clarity was poor (< 1 foot) and the weather was overcast. Further searching will be necessary to ascertain whether there is a lakewide zebra mussel population established in Long Lake.
